To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C-type lectins IRG-1 and IRG-7, which have been shown to be involved in innate immune response and pathogen resistance, also act as mediators of longevity induced by germ removal.
the C-type lectins IRG-7 and IRG-1 are required for the activation of the innate immune response and for the longevity of C. elegans animals exposed to live bacterial cells.
the C-type lectins IRG-7 and IRG-8 are required for the activation of DAF-16/DAF-12 and lifespan extension in animals lacking germ cells.

the mechanisms that control the lifespan of animals.
the mechanisms that underlie the association between the germline, immunity and longevity.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate the longevity of the nematode C. elegans.

the reproductive longevity pathway is an important mediator of innate immunity and that the somatic gonadal tissue can function as a signaling center that transmits information to the rest of animal to activate the immune response.
